def transform(grid):
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    n = len(grid)
    # A 5 at the bottom marks a column to extend upward. Existing colors
    # in that column partition it into runs, each extended upward to the
    # preceding source (or the top).
    markers = [j for j, value in enumerate(grid[-1]) if value == 5]
    for j in markers:
        sources = [(i, grid[i][j]) for i in range(n) if grid[i][j] not in (0, 5)]
        previous_end = 0
        for i, color in sources:
            for k in range(previous_end, i + 1):
                out[k][j] = color
            previous_end = i + 1
        for k in range(previous_end, n):
            out[k][j] = 5
    return out

def transform(grid):
    # Split around full-color-9 separator lines and columns.
    rs=[i for i,row in enumerate(grid) if all(x==9 for x in row)]
    cs=[j for j in range(len(grid[0])) if all(row[j]==9 for row in grid)]
    rb=[0]+[i+1 for i in rs]; re=rs+[len(grid)]
    cb=[0]+[j+1 for j in cs]; ce=cs+[len(grid[0])]
    out=[]
    for a,b in zip(rb,re):
        line=[]
        for c,d in zip(cb,ce):

        out.append(line)
    return out

def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter
    bg=Counter(x for row in grid for x in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    cells=[(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]!=bg]
    # Find the compact motif: largest connected non-background component excluding the isolated marker color.
    colors=Counter(grid[r][c] for r,c in cells)
    marker=max(colors, key=colors.get) if len(colors)>1 else None
    # In these puzzles marker is the repeated singleton color, while motif can itself have repeats.
    # Identify isolated points by connected components and choose largest component as motif.
    unseen=set(cells); comps=[]
    while unseen:
        st=[unseen.pop()]; comp=set(st)
        while st:
            r,c=st.pop()
            for q in ((r-1,c),(r+1,c),(r,c-1),(r,c+1)):
                if q in unseen: unseen.remove(q); comp.add(q); st.append(q)
        comps.append(comp)
    # Largest connected component is motif; if marker touches nothing it is singleton.
    motif=max(comps,key=len)
    rs=[r for r,c in motif]; cs=[c for r,c in motif]
    r0,r1,c0,c1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs)
    stamp=[row[c0:c1+1] for row in grid[r0:r1+1]]
    cr=(r1-r0)//2; cc=(c1-c0)//2
    points=[(r,c) for r,c in cells if (r,c) not in motif]
    out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    for r,c in points:
        for i,row in enumerate(stamp):
            for j,v in enumerate(row):
                rr,xx=r+i-cr,c+j-cc
                if 0<=rr<h and 0<=xx<w: out[rr][xx]=v
    return out
